headline: Sterling is about 1.3067 dollars on Wednesday evening, having dipped to about 1.3043 while Bank of England policymakers gave evidence to MPs and then recovered, still above Monday's low near 1.3011. US growth and inflation figures this afternoon came in above forecast, markets put about a 97% chance on a quarter point Fed rise on 9 December, and US markets are shut on Thursday for Thanksgiving.

drivers.title: The Fed
drivers.text: CME FedWatch figures quoted on 25 November put about a 97% chance on a quarter point rise from the present 3.75% to 4% range at the Fed meeting on 8 and 9 December, and about 66% on a further rise in January. New York Fed President John Williams said on 23 November that inflation is still too high, and BlackRock said on 24 November that it expects a December rise and one more in the first half of 2027.

drivers.title: The gap between US and UK rates
drivers.text: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 November, and a quarter point Fed rise in December would take US rates above UK rates. Bank of England policymaker Megan Greene said on 24 November that falls in inflation have stalled, which keeps a December Bank of England rise in play and gives the pound some support.

drivers.title: A strong dollar
drivers.text: The dollar index reached about 104.5 on Monday 23 November, its highest level since April 2025, then fell 0.44% on Tuesday to about 103.85 as US Treasury yields slipped. GBP/USD has fallen about 3% from a high near 1.3500 on 4 November, and the move has been mostly dollar strength rather than UK news.

drivers.title: US tariffs and share prices
drivers.text: Reuters reported on 24 November that the US Trade Representative is preparing findings of a probe into excess industrial capacity among 16 trading partners, including China and the European Union, which could lead to new tariffs. The dollar fell on Tuesday as US technology shares dropped on the news, then firmed on Wednesday morning as Asian shares fell, so the effect on the dollar has run both ways.

drivers.title: Oil and the Gulf
drivers.text: Brent oil settled more than 2% higher on 24 November on reports of new attacks on ships in and around the Strait of Hormuz, and opened at $90.97 a barrel (about £69.50) on 25 November. Dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound.

lower: Hotter than expected US core PCE inflation or stronger than expected growth figures this afternoon, which would support bets on more Fed rises and mean fewer dirhams per pound.
Further sharp falls in shares on tariff worries, or fresh attacks on shipping in the Gulf, which tend to send investors towards the dollar.
higher: Softer than expected US core PCE inflation or weaker growth figures this afternoon, which would ease bets on further Fed rises and mean more dirhams per pound.
Firm UK news or Bank of England comments that keep a December rise in play, which would lift the pound.
watch: No further scheduled US or UK figures are listed for the rest of this week, and US markets are shut on Thursday for Thanksgiving. The next big event is the Fed's decision on 9 December, where markets already expect a quarter point rise; any sign the Fed might hold back would tend to weaken the dollar and help someone selling pounds for dirhams.

feed.title: Sterling has recovered its dip during the Bank of England hearing
feed.text: The pound fell a little further after the last update, to a low of about 1.3043 at 18:42 Dubai, while Governor Bailey and other members of the Bank's rate-setting committee were still giving evidence to MPs, then climbed back to about 1.3067 by 19:08 and was near 1.3067 at 19:38. The move was again the pound's own, since EUR/USD drifted slightly lower over the same hour, from about 1.0945 to about 1.0940, so it points to UK news rather than the dollar. No report read yet says what the Bank's policymakers told MPs, so the cause of the dip and the recovery is not known; before the hearing, LSEG data cited by Reuters put about an 80% chance on a further Bank of England rise in December, and dirhams per pound are now back near where they were before the hearing began.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped while the Bank of England faces MPs
feed.text: Governor Bailey and three other members of the Bank's rate-setting committee began giving evidence to the Treasury Committee on the November Monetary Policy Report at 18:15 Dubai, but no report read yet says what they told MPs. A hint that the Bank is in less of a hurry to raise rates again would tend to weigh on the pound, and the move was the pound's own rather than the dollar's: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3068 at 18:23 Dubai to about 1.3052 by 18:38, while EUR/USD held steady near 1.0946, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: US growth and inflation have come in above forecast
feed.text: The second estimate put US growth in the third quarter at an annual rate of 4.3%, well above the 3.5% expected and up from 3.4% in the first estimate, and core PCE inflation for October rose 0.3% on the month as forecast but 3.3% on the year against 3.2% expected. Faster growth and firmer inflation usually support the case for Fed rises, which tends to strengthen the dollar and mean fewer dirhams per pound. In the event the dollar weakened slightly at first: GBP/USD dipped to about 1.3062 at the release, rose to about 1.3076 within a minute, then settled back near 1.3067 by 17:40 Dubai, and none of the sources checked explains the first move up.

feed.title: Sterling has edged back up as the dollar eases before the US figures
feed.text: The dollar gave back part of its morning gain in the hour before the US inflation and growth figures at 17:30 Dubai, falling against the euro as well as the pound, but none of the news sources checked names a cause for the move. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3055 at 16:03 Dubai to a high of about 1.3077 at 16:21, then settled near 1.3068 by 16:38, and EUR/USD rose by a similar share over the same minutes, which means slightly more dirhams per pound.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped further as the dollar firms ahead of US inflation figures
feed.text: The dollar has held firmer through the European morning, with the dollar index above 104 and up about 0.2% on the day, FXStreet reported, as markets wait for US core PCE inflation at 17:30 Dubai, expected to rise to 3.2% a year from 3.1%. GBP/USD moved between about 1.3066 and 1.3079 from 10:40 to 13:16 Dubai, then fell to about 1.3060 by 13:34, a larger fall than the euro's, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. FXStreet listed a Treasury Committee hearing on the Bank of England's November report with Governor Bailey for today, but no report read explains the drop at 13:20 Dubai, so its cause is not known.

feed.title: The dollar has edged higher as the Asian share sell-off deepens
feed.text: The fall in Asian shares deepened through Wednesday morning, with Taiwan's main index down 7.4%, South Korea's KOSPI down 6% and Japan's Nikkei down 3.3%, Investing.com reported, as worries about planned US tariffs on 16 trading partners and about AI spending hit chip makers; investors bought US government bonds, and markets still see a Fed rise on 9 December as almost certain. Sharp share falls and a firm Fed outlook both tend to draw money into the dollar, and it crept up against the pound and the euro by similar shares, so this was the dollar firming rather than UK news: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3088 at 07:40 Dubai to about 1.3079 at 09:40 and a low of about 1.3073 at 10:15, and was near 1.3076 at 10:30, while EUR/USD slipped from about 1.0943 to about 1.0933, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names a single new cause for this morning's drift, and traders are waiting for US inflation and growth figures at 17:30 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped as Asian shares fall on US tariff worries
feed.text: Asian shares fell sharply on Wednesday morning, with the MSCI Asia-Pacific index outside Japan down 2.3% and South Korea and Taiwan down more than 5% at worst, after Reuters reported that the US Trade Representative is preparing findings of a probe into excess capacity among 16 trading partners, and after the Nasdaq fell 1.5% overnight. Sharp falls in shares tend to send investors towards the dollar, and it edged up against both the pound and the euro: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3111 at the last update to about 1.3107 at 04:00 Dubai, then to about 1.3094 by 07:00 and was near 1.3092 at 07:38, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, so dirhams per pound are slightly lower. Brent oil opened 0.5% lower at $90.97 a barrel (about £69.50) after settling more than 2% higher on Tuesday on reports of fresh attacks on ships around the Strait of Hormuz.

feed.title: Sterling has held its gains as US yields slip on the tariff reports
feed.text: Weaker US shares after the reports of new US tariffs pushed investors into government bonds, and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to about 4.88%, its lowest since 10 November, FXStreet reported, which leaves the dollar index near 103.77 against Monday's 20-month high of 104.53. Lower US yields make the dollar less rewarding to hold, but markets still price a quarter point Fed rise on 9 December, so the dollar has eased only a little rather than fallen. GBP/USD dipped to a low of about 1.3096 at 19:42 Dubai, rose to a high of about 1.3121 at 21:57 and was near 1.3111 at 23:39, a little above about 1.3105 at the last update, so dirhams per pound are slightly higher.

feed.title: US consumer confidence has jumped well above forecasts
feed.text: The Conference Board's consumer confidence index rose to 103.3 in November, its highest since January 2025, against about 92.4 expected and 91.9 in October, with the Conference Board pointing to less uncertainty after the midterm elections and lower petrol prices. A stronger US consumer supports the case for further Fed rises and so tends to firm the dollar, but the reaction was small: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3110 at 19:00 Dubai to a low of about 1.3100 by 19:15, then recovered to about 1.3110 by 19:27 and was near 1.3106 at 19:38, so dirhams per pound are little changed. FXStreet reported that the dollar index stayed below 104.00, as the losses that followed the tariff reports earlier this evening outweighed the strong figure.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened after reports of new US tariffs
feed.text: The Wall Street Journal reported at about 17:38 Dubai that the US is preparing higher tariffs on China, the European Union and 14 other trading partners, and US share futures fell sharply, with Nasdaq futures down about 2.4%, FXStreet reported. The dollar's recent strength has leaned on a rally in US technology shares, and it gave ground across the board as they fell: GBP/USD rose steadily from about 1.3089 at 17:34 Dubai to about 1.3108 by 18:39, and EUR/USD by a slightly larger share, which means more dirhams per pound. Bank of England policymaker Megan Greene said earlier that falls in inflation have stalled and argued for another rise, and a weekly ADP reading showed slower US private hiring, but neither moved the rate at the time.

feed.title: The dollar has slipped as the euro firms on talk of an ECB rise
feed.text: ECB policymaker Gediminas Simkus said on Tuesday that the central bank should act sooner rather than later and called the weak euro another inflationary factor, after German business confidence rose for a seventh month to 90.6 against 90.5 expected, FXStreet reported. The euro is the largest weight in the dollar index, so a firmer euro pulled the dollar back across the board: EUR/USD rose from about 1.0930 at 14:40 Dubai to about 1.0955, and GBP/USD climbed steadily from about 1.3064 to about 1.3087 by 16:38, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names a US cause, and the dollar remains near its strongest since April 2025 ahead of US consumer confidence at 19:00 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has eased a little across the board, with no clear cause
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3047 at 13:00 Dubai to a high of about 1.3070 at 14:10 and was near 1.3061 at 14:35, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share, from about 1.0915 to about 1.0931, so this was the dollar giving back a little ground rather than the pound rising on UK news, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. German business confidence improved in November, investingLive reported, which may have helped the euro, but no report read names a US or UK cause, and the dollar remains close to its strongest since early 2025 ahead of US consumer confidence this evening.

feed.title: Sterling has edged up in quiet London trade as the dollar holds firm
feed.text: GBP/USD dipped to a low of about 1.3027 at 11:00 Dubai as London opened, then rose from about 1.3033 at 12:29 to about 1.3049 by 12:36 with no news that explains the move, and was near 1.3048 at 12:38, a little above about 1.3038 at the last update. The dollar is holding near its strongest since April 2025 despite the rebound in shares, with analysts pointing to Treasury yields and Fed rise bets, while Brent oil near $89 a barrel (about £68) sits close to a three-month low even after Iran said three tankers hit mines, which takes some support away from the dollar.

feed.title: Sterling has held steady overnight as the Fed's Williams keeps rises in play
feed.text: New York Fed President John Williams said on Monday evening that inflation is still too high, that he is not excluding Fed rises at consecutive meetings, but that the situation does not call for dramatic action, so markets still price a quarter point rise in December and no larger move. Comments that confirm what is already priced did little to the dollar: GBP/USD was about 1.3031 at 01:00 Dubai, edged up to about 1.3046 by 05:15 in quiet Asian trade and was near 1.3037 at 07:38, little changed from about 1.3029 at the last update.

feed.title: The dollar has eased back in late trading, with no clear cause
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3014 at 21:50 Dubai to about 1.3032 by 23:30 and was near 1.3029 at 23:38, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share, from about 1.0880 to about 1.0897, so this was the dollar giving back a little of today's rally across the board rather than the pound rising on UK news, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names the news behind the late easing; the dollar index had earlier reached its highest since April 2025, and New York Fed President John Williams speaks at 01:00 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has extended its rally as Fed rise bets firm
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3048 at 19:42 Dubai to about 1.3016 by 20:15, and was near 1.3020 at 20:36, while EUR/USD fell from about 1.0912 to about 1.0880 to its lowest since April 2025, so this was the dollar strengthening across the board rather than the pound falling on UK news. FXStreet linked the dollar's gains to the Nvidia-led rally in US shares after Jensen Huang was reinstated as chief executive, and to traders almost fully pricing a quarter point Fed rise in December. Higher expected US rates support the dollar, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: The dollar has kept rising despite softer US business surveys
feed.text: The US flash services survey for November fell to 54.7 against about 55.7 expected, manufacturing came in at 54.5 in line with forecasts, and the composite measure eased to 54.6 from 55.9, though S&P Global said its price gauges still point to inflation well above the Fed's 2% target. Softer US activity would usually weigh on the dollar, but the dollar index held near 104.2, its highest since April 2025, so the dollar kept firming across the board and there are slightly fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD was about 1.3059 at 18:44 Dubai, slid to about 1.3032 by 19:14 while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from about 1.0931 to about 1.0909, and was near 1.3046 at 19:38; no report read names a single cause for the extra dollar buying.

feed.title: The dollar has spiked and fallen back, with no clear cause
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3075 at 17:37 Dubai to about 1.3065 by 17:50, then dropped to about 1.3053 at 17:53 before recovering to about 1.3072 by 17:57, and was near 1.3065 at 18:37. EUR/USD fell by a larger share in the same minutes, from about 1.0940 to about 1.0909, and also recovered, so this was a brief burst of dollar buying across the board rather than the pound falling on UK news, which left slightly fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names the news behind the spike; CoinDesk reported the dollar index above 104, its highest since March 2025, about an hour earlier, and the US flash business surveys are due at 18:45 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has jumped across the board, with no clear cause yet
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3096 at 16:31 Dubai to about 1.3084 by 16:44, then fell quickly to about 1.3068 by 16:47, recovered to about 1.3080 at 17:00 and was near 1.3074 at 17:36. EUR/USD fell by a slightly larger share in the same minutes, from about 1.0961 to about 1.0933, so this was the dollar strengthening across the board rather than the pound weakening on UK news, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names the news behind the jump; investingLive described the euro sliding from 1.1005 to 1.0941 during the day as the dollar trades mixed, and the US flash business surveys are still due at 18:45 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has drifted lower as the dollar firms ahead of US surveys
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3116 at 13:45 Dubai to about 1.3101 by 14:20, briefly recovered to about 1.3109 at 14:45 and was near 1.3096 at 15:39, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from about 1.0975 to about 1.0959, so the dollar firmed across the board rather than the pound falling on UK news, which means slightly fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names the news behind this afternoon's drift; earlier on Monday FXStreet described the dollar as easing on a recovery in share futures, and the US flash business surveys are due at 18:45 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped after weaker UK business surveys
feed.text: The UK flash services survey for November fell to 52.0 against 53.0 expected, and the composite measure of private sector activity eased to 52.3 from 52.9, with both services and manufacturing slowing, FXStreet reported; no report read yet gives the manufacturing figure. Slower UK growth weakens the case for a December Bank of England rise, which weighs on the pound, so slightly fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD was about 1.3122 at 13:29 Dubai, fell to about 1.3115 by 13:31 and was near 1.3114 at 13:38, after drifting down from about 1.3139 at 12:42 as the dollar firmed across the board, with EUR/USD falling by a similar share from about 1.0993 to about 1.0978 before the figures.

feed.title: Sterling has risen further as European markets get going
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3117 at 12:23 Dubai to about 1.3135 by 12:38 and held near 1.3134 at 12:40, while EUR/USD rose by about half as much, from about 1.0985 to about 1.0993, so a softer dollar accounts for part of the move and the pound also gained on the euro, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names the news behind the move; it came as the German business surveys for November were due at 12:30 Dubai, but no report read yet gives their figures, and the UK surveys follow at 13:30 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has edged higher as the dollar eases further
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3101 at 08:40 Dubai to about 1.3119 by 10:10 and was near 1.3120 at 10:30, while EUR/USD rose by a similar share, from about 1.0975 to about 1.0991, so the dollar softened across the board rather than the pound gaining on UK news, which means slightly more dirhams per pound. No report read names a single item of news behind the move, which came before London opened; FXStreet earlier on Monday described the dollar retreating from its highest level in 19 months as traders take profits in a week shortened by Thanksgiving, and noted that US Treasury yields have fallen sharply.

feed.title: The dollar has eased as markets reopen with a relief rally
feed.text: US share futures jumped about 2% in early Asian trade on Monday after a weekend in which South Korea and China moved to steady their stock markets and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned the Fed against raising rates too far, investingLive reported, and the dollar eased against most major currencies. Traders have also pared bets on a large Fed rise: CME FedWatch puts the chance of a quarter point rise in December at 93.2%, down from 97.3% on Friday, and a half point rise, given an 11.5% chance a week ago, is no longer priced, FXStreet reported. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3057 in Kraken's late weekend price, below Friday's close near 1.3084, to about 1.3086 by 03:00 Dubai and about 1.3107 by 05:00, gaining more than EUR/USD, which rose from about 1.0962 to about 1.0979, so a softer dollar and support for the pound from last week's strong UK retail sales mean slightly more dirhams per pound.
